narration: Marlow never had to threaten anyone. He simply reminded them what they owed.

shots.exact_dialogue: Every man in this valley owes me something
shots.speaker: Marlow
shots.visual: Marlow on the porch at dusk, addressing the farmers.

narration: The harvest was never the point.

shots.exact_dialogue: I never wanted the harvest. I wanted the land it grew on.
shots.visual: Close on Marlow, wheat field behind him going out of focus.

narration: By the second season the debt had become the whole relationship.

shots.exact_dialogue: A debt isn't a rope. It's a road. It goes both directions.
shots.visual: Two men walking the frozen access road.

narration: Twice in one season, the same answer.

shots.visual: Wide shot of the field at night.

narration: The winter closes in on all of them at once.

shots.exact_dialogue: We ration from tonight. No exceptions.
shots.visual: Holt at the head of the table, lamp swinging.

narration: Nobody gets out of that county untouched.
The field itself does the talking.

shots.nearest_dialogue: You can't bury a thing that keeps growing back
shots.visual: Slow aerial over the burnt field at sunrise. No dialogue.

narration: Another story ends the same way.

shots.exact_dialogue: You never asked me what it cost

shots.visual: Macro of frost forming on soil. No dialogue anywhere near.
